Subject: Packaging and marginal-recapture clause — pricing exhibit redline

Sanjay —

Thanks again for the productive demo last week. As we discussed on the call, Brightline's packaging mix (bursting in/out of higher-volume SKUs) creates a risk where a small downward shift in committed packaging can meaningfully change effective unit economics for Redwood. To keep seller economics intact while still giving Brightline flexibility, our legal team proposed a short "marginal recapture" mechanism in Exhibit B of the order form.

I've attached our first-pass redline (pricing-exhibit_redline_v1.docx). High level: when monthly realized effective unit price for invoiced units falls below the contracted floor because of SKU reclassification or packaging shifts, Redwood may reclaim the delta on the marginal units up to a capped percentage of ARR for the quarter. This is intended as an anti-gaming / stabilization mechanism, not a penalty.

Can you take a look and let me know your preferred times for a quick 30-min sync next week? If you prefer, we can also iterate directly on the redline and push a consolidated version for signature.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0117

Attachments: pricing-exhibit_redline_v1.docx (Word redline of Exhibit B)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@brightlinelabs.com>

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Packaging and marginal-recapture clause — pricing exhibit redline

Jordan —

Appreciate the background and the redline. Procurement and legal reviewed and we have a few immediate concerns:

- The proposed recapture is open-ended as drafted; Brightline will push back on any mechanism that allows retroactive invoice adjustments without a strict cap and a defined lookback window.
- We need a clear carve-out for contract renewals and for customers on grandfathered pricing (existing customers shouldn't be subject to a new recapture that changes past committed economics).
- Can the cap be expressed as a percentage of ARR per rolling 12 months (we'd propose 3%) rather than an absolute dollar cap?

I've attached our annotated comments (BL-pricing-comments.pdf) — see pages 2–3 for suggested alternative language. If Redwood can limit exposure and narrow the language, we can proceed. Otherwise procurement will request removal.

I'm available for a 30-min call Thursday 11/12 10am ET or Friday 11/13 2pm ET.

—Sanjay Rao
Head of Procurement | Brightline Labs
sanjay.rao@brightlinelabs.com

Attachment: BL-pricing-comments.pdf

Subject: RE: Packaging and marginal-recapture clause — pricing exhibit redline

Jordan / Marissa —

I reviewed the redline and Sanjay's annotated comments. Procurement's pushback is predictable; we should aim for a middle ground that preserves revenue protection while addressing commercial and auditability concerns. Quick summary and recommendation:

Risk summary:
- Ambiguity around the trigger and computation may invite disputes.
- Broad retroactive recapture can be construed as a billing adjustment requiring specific notice and refund mechanics under some customers' rules.

Recommended redline (replace the current Marginal Recapture paragraph in Exhibit B with the language below):

"Marginal Recapture. If, in any billing month, the Customer's invoiced effective unit price for Product SKUs subject to this Order falls below the Contracted Floor due solely to (i) the Customer's voluntary reclassification of usage among packaged SKUs or (ii) the Customer's material reduction in packaged commitment within the immediately preceding 90-day period (each a 'Trigger Event'), Redwood may invoice and recover, on a prospective basis only, the difference between the Contracted Floor and the invoiced effective unit price on the marginal units that gave rise to the shortfall, subject to the following limitations: (A) Redwood's aggregate recapture in any rolling 12-month period shall not exceed four percent (4%) of the Customer's annual recurring revenue under this Order; (B) Recapture shall not be applied to Renewals for which pricing was agreed prior to the Trigger Event; and (C) no recapture shall be charged more than 180 days after the applicable Trigger Event.

This language narrows scope (90-day lookback), adds a quantifiable cap (4% ARR rolling 12 months), excludes renewals, and limits the window for chargeback. It is operationally implementable and defensible in audit.

Operational asks: finance needs the formula for computing 'invoiced effective unit price' (we should align on token/unit mapping and a sample calc). Marissa — can you prepare a one-pager with a sample computation using Brightline's projected mix and send to Sanjay?

If Jordan is comfortable with the 4% cap we can present this consolidated redline back to Brightline. If they insist on 3%, we can evaluate trade-offs (e.g., keep 4% but narrow the recapture to only marginal units above a de minimis band).

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Kim / Marissa —

Thanks, Kim — that language reads well and addresses the core concerns. I'm OK presenting the 4% rolling cap as long as we add a grandfathering bullet for current committed SKUs (customers under existing volume commitments prior to the Effective Date). Suggest we:

1) Keep Kim's draft verbatim but add: "For the avoidance of doubt, Customers with a Commencement Date prior to the Effective Date of this Order shall not be subject to Marginal Recapture with respect to SKU commitments agreed prior to such Commencement Date."
2) Provide a one-page sample calc (Marissa, can you draft) and include a worked example in the redline doc so procurement can validate the number.

I'll hold the call invites until I hear whether Sanjay prefers Thurs or Fri. If they push to 3% we should table a concession: keep 4% but shorten the lookback to 60 days or add a de minimis threshold (e.g., recapture only when monthly effective unit variance > 5%).

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
